notes: Seven tons follows the explicit user correction; the older six-ton source statement remains superseded.
Single canopy-free side elevation, compact bottom strip and no right rail follow the latest explicit user layout request.
MERL Fowler S1021 is an archival drafting/composition reference, not evidence for the shape or dimensions of No. 5499.
The side geometry is analytically redrafted against actual No. 5499 photographs: straight barrel edges, circular wheel faces, shared fork/axle anchors and joined steering paths.
Proportions, repeated fasteners and spokes are interpreted; no surveyed dimensions, manufacturing tolerances or internal construction are asserted.
The source blueprint used White 0.30/0.40/0.50 mm pens on blue stock. The compact user-authorised composition adds named heritage zones without changing the shared format-v1 file.

Small drafted circles retain their radii during projection. Spoke corners use tangent fillets; shafts and fittings share local centres. Chain connectors meet their link ends, and closed contours are joined across the authoring seam before sub-nib filtering.
Revision 6 adds the user-requested separate Invicta casting and an enlarged oval worksplate in the clear top-right space; the small engine plate has no lettering.

Revisions 6-13 used the Preston Services casting photograph for the Invicta silhouette and selected reliefs. Revision 14 supersedes that horse drawing with the user-selected GWRA lot 51 casting photograph.

The GWRA reference is worksplate 6882. Its oval aspect and text layout are adapted to user-confirmed 5499. Text is redrawn for reliable single-line plotting, not claimed as a facsimile of the hand-engraved letterforms.

The chimney now widens upward. The forward rear-wheel scraper is reconstructed from the retained engine photographs; the matching far-side scraper is coincident and hidden in the strict side projection.

The far-side steering handwheel now has an open elliptical rim and three connected spokes. Its major-axis inclination follows the side photo; the finite visible width is interpreted using the front video frame.

Both road wheels now show staggered inner spokes behind the inclined outer cast spokes. Circular rims and coaxial hubs are unchanged. Obscured construction and spoke angles are interpreted to express the requested diagonal overlap, not asserted as factory geometry.
Revision 7 reduces the steering handwheel to approximately half its previous diameter and shows a diagonal shaft toward the far-side steering gear, occluded by intervening engine parts.

The near chain now runs from the lower winding-gear exit to the visible front scraper bracket. The far chain uses the upper exit on the opposite side and the corresponding hidden front bracket; it is drawn behind the engine, winding-gear casing and complete front roll.
A small V-shaped squeeze-release handle is attached to the quadrant lever, following the source photo and user correction.

Revision 8 supersedes the earlier oblique steering-wheel display with an edge-on rim and hub, moved slightly toward the engine body. The shaft is concealed behind the complete rear-assembly silhouette.
The oval boiler fitting and its connected spindle/lever move left together and are enlarged clear of both adjacent bands.
Chain front anchors now coincide with the leading spring tensioner output eyes, on their respective sides. The older trailing-bracket attachments are removed.

Ten rear and six front spokes per set, deeper annular rims and 0.50 mm outer rim outlines follow the requested visual simplification. These counts are an illustrative choice, not dimensional verification.

Printed footer retains manufacturer, model, works number, registration and year only. Ownership, weight and NTS notation are omitted from the artwork as requested; interpretive scope remains documented here.

Revision 9 removes all six wheel-perimeter centre guides. Single-stroke text is checked against the bundled plotter-grid-v4 font, the eight-nib cap floor and three-nib stroke floor. All paths use the configured White blueprint 0.30/0.40/0.50 mm inventory; the engine geometry and printed copy are retained.

Final revision 10 gives the existing return-pipe walls an opaque tube mask so the far chain is hidden at their crossing. The ground datum below the rollers is removed. All remaining engine geometry, lettering, pen sizes and layout are retained.

Revision 11 lowers the complete engine by one A3 format gap (6 mm) without scaling it. The horse and worksplate group is enlarged uniformly by 10 percent about its top-right layout anchor, with pen widths retained at their physical sizes.

Revision 12 places the worksplate to the left of the Invicta horse, vertically centred as a pair. Relative to revision 11, the worksplate is 20 percent larger and the horse 50 percent larger, retaining their aspect ratios and physical pen widths. The rear firebox wall joins the upper control-housing edge directly and turns into the rear deck with a tangent quarter-circle, replacing the diagonal gap behind the rear wheel.

Revision 13 restores the lower quadrant-lever blade, on the same axis as the existing handle. The retained actual-engine photograph shows it continuing below the notched quadrant and behind the rear wheel. Its lower construction end enters the existing rear-frame mask; the pivot and internal mechanism remain concealed, rather than being invented as visible hardware. All previous paths and layout remain unchanged.

Revision 14 replaces the previous Invicta outline with the user-selected GWRA March 2025 lot 51 casting. The photograph constrains the silhouette and sculpted detail. In-plane rotation sets the casting upright; smooth cubic contour and relief paths are drawn with the existing White 0.30/0.40 mm pens. The engine, worksplate, footer and page composition are retained.

Colour edition 5: the 863 revision-14 paths are kept unchanged in shape, except the regulator rod, redrawn straight and level with a neat bend down onto the motion plate (8 paths reshaped, 2 removed). The black lines are drawn with the studio's one black pen, 0.25 mm: engine linework is one weight heavier than the blueprint (0.40/0.60 mm, roller tyres 1.00 mm), each heavier line built from 0.25 mm loops round its path; fasteners, chains, small fittings, scrapers, lettering, badges and frame keep their original weights. The inner lines of the three brass boiler bands (four paths) are drawn in Gold.

Colour is added only as single-pass pen lines inside the enclosed paper cells, kept at least 0.22 mm clear of black ink. The Gold band inner lines meet black ink only at their ends and where they cross the boiler lines, as the blueprint draws them.

Open air stays paper: under the regulator rod on both sides of the flywheel and between the lubricator pedestal and its pipe. The boiler barrel seen between the motion plate and the pump rod beside the flywheel is green, and the gold band nearest the flywheel runs up to the motion plate.

The wheels, hubs and flywheel are black iron drawn as close, even Black circles. Everything seen through the rear wheel up to the tender front edge is black iron in Black lines about 0.69 mm apart, lighter than the black wheels; the green tender continues beyond that edge.

Spokes are ruled with a fixed number of lines exactly parallel to their edges. Cylinders are graded lines under upper-left light. The fork, scrapers, scraper mounts and chain spring bar are red-brown: Red lines with a Brown line in every gap, 0.30 mm apart, so the red reads darker and warmer.
Black-painted iron (chimney, smokebox, headstock, firebox, fittings and controls) is hatched in Black alone, its tone set by line spacing; the studio has no grey pen.

The worksplate and Invicta horse at the top right are left as black engraving without colour. The boiler bands, valves, whistle and the maker plate on the cylinder are brass, built from fine lines with the studio Gold 0.40 mm pen; there is no broad gold nib. Each boiler band is a solid gold bar of upright lines evenly spaced about 0.42 mm apart from one black edge to the other, its inner line drawn in Gold as one of them; the lines run unbroken from end to end of the band, under the black boiler lines that cross it, stopping only where the pump rod passes in front. The valves, whistle and maker plate are lined 0.50 mm apart.
